What Is A Dirty Bomb?
A dirty bomb is a conventional explosive device combined with radioactive material.
It differs from a nuclear bomb because a regular explosive is used rather than creating a nuclear chain reaction.
A dirty bomb could impact several city blocks, whereas a nuclear blast would vaporize much of a city.

title: Japan sends up jets after alleged Russian incursion of its airspace
summary:
Japan says it launched fighter jets and "strongly" protested after two suspected Russian aircraft violated its airspace early on Tuesday.
South Korea also says it deployed fighter jets, while Taiwan says it "responded" to Russian military aircraft detected in their respective air defence identification zones.
The last such incursion was in 2024, when a Russian military patrol plane entered Japanese airspace off Rebun island, Hokkaido.
Taiwan says its military "responded accordingly" after two Russian military aircraft entered its air defence identification zone, also on Tuesday.
South Korea says it sent up jets after an unspecified number of Russian military aircraft entered its air defence identification zone over the Sea of Japan.

title: Trump announces critical minerals agreements at Quad meeting in Manila
summary:
US President Trump said the deals would prevent ‘coercion by any single foreign supplier’.
United States President Donald Trump says that members of the Quad, a security grouping of the US and three Indo-Pacific countries, have reached agreements aimed at securing supply chains of critical minerals.
Trump met India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Australia’s Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi – the other Quad leaders – in the Philippines on Thursday.
During the meeting, Trump said the agreements on critical minerals aimed to prevent “coercion by any single foreign supplier”.
In a statement after the leaders’ meeting, the Quad expressed “grave concerns” about “economic coercion”, including through arbitrary export restrictions.

title: Rebeca Grynspan could be the UN’s first woman boss, if she can sway Trump
summary:
Share Rebecca Grynspan could be the UN’s first woman boss, if she can sway Trump on social mediaIn straw poll after straw poll among members of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) to choose the organisation’s next leader, one name keeps emerging ahead of all others: Costa Rican diplomat Rebeca Grynspan.
If Grynspan, 70, beats out the other candidates, the current head of the UN’s top trade body would become the world’s first woman and the first Jewish person to hold the post of UN secretary-general.
And she’ll need to win over one leader above all, who has demonstrated his desire to dismantle the very UN Grynspan hopes to lead: United States President Donald Trump.
She took on its reins, promising post-COVID economic recovery, supporting digital transitions, and aligning with UN goals on climate change.
“What my identity gives me is empathy, not bias,” Grynspan said to Al Jazeera.
